name: GCSE Geography (AQA 8035)

selected_options.uk_physical_landscapes_options: Coastal landscapes AND Glacial landscapes (not River landscapes)
selected_options.resource_management_option: Water — the school's booklet did not confirm which of Food/Water/Energy is taught in depth; the user was unsure, so this course builds Water as the most commonly taught AQA option nationally. Can be swapped for Food or Energy later if the school confirms otherwise.
selected_options.case_studies: NEE city: Lagos, Nigeria. UK city: Manchester. Changing economic world case study country: Nigeria. All three confirmed from the school's own booklet.
selected_options.fieldwork: Two fieldwork enquiries used as this course's worked examples: Cleveleys (coastal management) and Salford Quays (urban regeneration).

material_vintage: AQA GCSE Geography (8035) specification, first teaching 2016, current and live; itemised on 2026-09-22 from the AQA specification PDF (subject content 3.1-3.4, assessment objectives in section 4, scheme of assessment) fetched directly on this date, which confirmed: the AO weightings (AO1 15%, AO2 25%, AO3 35% incl. minimum 10% fieldwork, AO4 25% incl. minimum 5% fieldwork), the three-paper scheme (Paper 1 and Paper 2 each 1 hour 30 minutes/88 marks/35%, Paper 3 1 hour 30 minutes/76 marks/30%), and the option structure (Living World: Ecosystems and Tropical rainforests compulsory, then Hot deserts OR Cold environments; UK physical landscapes: overview compulsory, then any two of Coastal/River/Glacial; Resource management: overview compulsory, then one of Food/Water/Energy). Named case studies and figures (Chile 2010, Nepal 2015, Typhoon Haiyan 2013, Storm Desmond 2015, Amazon deforestation, Alaska, Purbeck/Dorset, Cleveleys and Medmerry, the Lake District, Lagos, Manchester and Salford Quays, Jamaica tourism, Nigeria, Lesotho Highlands Water Project and Kenyan sand dams) reflect the well-established named examples used in AQA-aligned teaching of this specification; exact current statistics (death tolls, magnitudes, rainfall and cost figures) are given at the commonly cited order of magnitude from training knowledge and are flagged here for re-verification against primary sources (e.g. USGS, national disaster reports) rather than confirmed against a live page on this date. The AQA-published November 2020 Paper 2 (8035/2) mark scheme was used for the generic levels-of-response band wording, carried over unchanged from the original build.
level_source: RQF Level 2 (GCSE, full grade range 1-9 / Foundation+Higher tiers covered), per Ofqual's Register of Regulated Qualifications listing for this specification
framework: AQA three-level generic levels-of-response bands for extended questions (Level 1 basic 1-3, Level 2 clear, Level 3 detailed, scaled to the question's total marks), combining AO1 knowledge, AO2 understanding, and AO3 application/analysis/evaluation
